assign.now: change 4 applied - the append helper replaces the encoding, clock and re-parse prose

log.msg: Measured BEFORE (wc -l): minion 74, new-task 108, code 177, finish-task 84, mastermind 386, CLAUDE.md 43. A fresh minion before its first write loads minion + new-task + code = 359 lines (402 with CLAUDE.md). The tiers-design figure of 427 was measured against slightly older files; 359 is this session's own baseline.

Change 4 applied (the append helper). new-task 108 -> 92 (-16), finish-task 84 -> 70 (-14), minion 74 -> 74 (one long bullet rewritten, no line change), code 177 -> 177 (the heredoc bullet is one very long line, so wc -l cannot see the cut). Five passages of BOM / ANSI / clock-drift / escape / re-parse prose became one sentence each naming .claude/hooks/append.mjs.

MEASUREMENT CAVEAT worth carrying: wc -l badly under-measures code/SKILL.md, whose section 7 bullets are one very long line each - 177 lines but 24,977 characters. Characters (and so tokens) are the honest second dimension; both are reported on the page.

decision.topic: the heredoc trap in minion and code
decision.chose: kept the heredoc rule as a rule, only folded its jsonl half into append.mjs
options: delete the heredoc bullets outright, as change 4's text literally says
keep the rule, name append.mjs for the jsonl half
decision.why: append.mjs only covers appending to a .jsonl. The heredoc trap is about writing ANY file from the shell - an edit script, a python block, a ui-test plan - so deleting the bullet would have lost a live rule that has cost five tasks a retry apiece.

assign.now: changes 5, 2 and 1 applied; measuring and then the lean always-loaded set

log.msg: Change 5 applied (a trap is one sentence and a link). code 177 -> 196 lines but 3,908 -> 3,166 words and 24,977 -> 20,668 chars; minion 74 -> 68; new-task 92 -> 87; mastermind 386 -> 382. code's LINE count rose because section 7 gained seven one-line group headings (Names that collide with core / The ambient captor / Config fields / Timing and lifecycle / Blast radius / Layout and CSS / The tools themselves) - the audit's own complaint was that a rule is unfindable in a wall, so the headings are the fix, and words are the honest measure of what an agent reads.

FINDING that changes how change 5 should be applied anywhere else: the audit assumed every trap's story is already in a task log, so the story could be replaced by a link. Checked all 20 cited tasks mechanically (keyword of the trap against every file in the task dir): 16 hold it, 4 do not - paging-clarity (the naming() collision), list-shapes (the captor return value and the details toggle loop), even-columns (mixed CRLF), real-page-move (the python truncating one-liner). Those four keep their full paragraph inline, per the brief's rule that detail is never deleted. The other 16 became rule + check + link.

Change 2 applied (the Agent-tool era leaves the mastermind skill). The foreground rule for Agent-tool sub-masterminds, the SendMessage-a-parked-worker bullet and the vanishing-transcript bullet became two lines pointing at tiers-design/doc/roles.md and the sub-mastermind skill; the mastermind's identity is its Servex agent id or session uuid, not a ListAgents name. 382 -> 371 lines. Grep confirms no SendMessage, ListAgents or run_in_background guidance is left in either skill.

Change 1 (superseded) applied. The 35-line 'A minion is a CLI session with its own id' section became a 9-line 'Spawning - spawn_agent on Servex, the CLI as the fallback': spawn/send/interrupt/stop/list as MCP tools with role-loads-the-skill and the parent-wake, the full CLI command kept as the fallback with its two permission flags, and the record rule. 371 -> 343 lines.

assign.now: measured both ways and proved nothing broke; writing the page

log.msg: The lean always-loaded set applied to minion. minion now states in one line what it carries by default (itself + new-task) and lists everything else as read-X-when-Y: code before the first JS edit, layout before anything with a size, css/new-css-class before a declaration or a new name, new-page before a page.js, ui-test to prove a gesture, research before recording a finding, documentation then finish-task at landing. The reload-hold section went from seven dense lines to four and now links reload-hold for the design. 68 -> 70 lines, 2025 -> 1907 words.

THE TWO NUMBERS, and they agree. Method 1, wc -l on minion + new-task + code: 359 lines before, 353 after. Method 2, load-count.mjs, which parses minion/SKILL.md for the sentence naming what it carries by default and sums only those files plus code: 353 lines, identical. In words the same three files went 7,604 -> 6,294 (-17%); in characters 48,108 -> 40,710 (-15%). The script is public/framework/ai/2026-09-22/skills-shrink-2/load-count.mjs.

WHY THE 200-LINE TARGET WAS NOT MET, provably. These files wrap a whole paragraph onto one physical line, so wc -l does not measure what an agent reads: code/SKILL.md is 196 lines holding 3,166 words, and section 7 alone is 58 lines holding 2,080. Sections 1-6 and 8 of code - which the tiers-design audit itself says earn every line - are 138 lines. So minion (70) + new-task (87) + code with section 7 DELETED ENTIRELY (138) = 295 lines, still 95 over the target, without a single trap left in the file. The target was unreachable by construction. Measured in words, the thing an agent actually pays for, the cut is 17 percent and every rule and every story survived.

Proof nothing broke, three ways. (1) Frontmatter: all five edited SKILL.md files parse with a name and a description. (2) The Skill tool lists them: a Haiku session asked for its skills returned code, finish-task, mastermind, minion and new-task among 21 repo skills. (3) A live Haiku minion launched with the CLI recipe on a two-line brief in this task dir loaded the minion skill, wrote hello.txt and landed - 5 turns, 9.4 seconds, $0.058, session b24cbd8e-2082-490f-96dd-e53816aa1038.

Improvements entries deleted because this task applied them: code x2 (backticks are all p() reads; an Edit that opens a capture callback must close it in the same Edit), minion x5 (Playwright is a global module, import it by file url; the hold expires mid-batch so re-issue it and take a fresh one per batch; the hold does not cover a save under Server/; the boot test is the ROOT server.js; cmd /c start opens dialogs on the owner's desktop, and a refused call means change HOW you call it). One new entry filed on mastermind: measure a skill in words, not lines, before setting a shrink target.

decision.topic: 09-19 change 3 - who owns the improvements loop
decision.chose: left the text untouched; recommending the merge
options: merge auditor into master-assistant and let that role edit the skills (change 3 as written)
keep auditor separate so supervision stays cheap to re-read (the 2026-09-17 skill-roles decision)
decision.why: This is the owner's call about what a role IS, not a fail-safe edit, and master-assistant and auditor are outside this task's fence either way. The recommendation is to merge: the backlog this task just worked through had entries up to five weeks old that nobody owned, and the two skills both call themselves the system architect. The caveat the original decision named still holds - if the merged audit section grows past one screen, link its history rather than carrying it.

decision.topic: traps whose story is not in the task log the audit assumed
decision.chose: kept the full paragraph inline for the four that failed the check
options: shrink every trap to one sentence and a link, as change 5 reads
shrink only where the linked log demonstrably holds the story
decision.why: The brief's own rule is that detail is never deleted, and four of the twenty cited tasks (paging-clarity, list-shapes, even-columns, real-page-move) do not mention their trap anywhere in the task dir. Linking those would have quietly destroyed the only copy. The check is mechanical and cheap - a keyword of the trap against every file in the task dir - and is worth running before any future pass of this kind.

decision.topic: the numbers the owner chose and the never-lists earned by breakage
decision.chose: left every one of them exactly as written
options: tighten or re-harden rules while shrinking
shrink prose only, never a rule
decision.why: The mastermind skill's own house rule: a hard rule is earned by breaking things repeatedly, and the owner deliberately softened two numeric rules on 2026-08-18 because agents were treating thresholds as verdicts. Nothing in this pass changed what a skill DECIDES - only how much text a decision is wrapped in. The one addition is a clause the servex-integrate improvements entry asked for, which restates an existing rule rather than making a new one.

assign.outcome:
**The skill changes that were written down twice and applied never are applied.** A fresh minion now reads **6,294 words** of instructions before its first write, down from 7,577 — 17% less — and not one rule, not one number the owner chose, and not one trap story was deleted to get there.

The report is the page: [**Skills shrink**](/framework/ai/2026-09-22/skills-shrink-2/) — three numbers, the before/after table for all five files, and what was deliberately left alone.

What changed, in order: `append.mjs` replaced the BOM, ANSI, clock-drift and re-parse prose in `new-task`, `finish-task`, `minion` and `code`; every trap that had a task log to point at became one sentence plus that link; the Agent-tool era left the `mastermind` skill; and its 35-line CLI launch recipe became 9 lines led by `spawn_agent` on Servex, with the CLI kept as the fallback. `minion` now says in one line what it carries by default and lists everything else as read-X-when-Y.

Proved three ways: all five files still parse with valid frontmatter; a Haiku session asked for its skills named all five; and a live Haiku minion launched with the CLI recipe on a two-line brief loaded the shrunk `minion` skill, wrote its file and landed in 9.4 seconds for six cents. The report page loads with zero console errors and zero failed requests.

**Two things a reader should know.** The ≤200-line target was unreachable by construction, not by effort: these files put a whole paragraph on one physical line, so `wc -l` never measured what an agent reads — with `code`'s entire trap section deleted the three files still total 295 lines. Words is the honest unit, and that correction is now filed against the mastermind skill. And the audit's premise that every trap story already lives in a task log is only 80% true: four of twenty cited tasks do not mention their trap anywhere, so those four keep their full paragraph rather than lose the only copy.

Left as decisions, not edits: who owns the improvements loop (recommendation: merge the auditor into the master assistant), and every number and never-list the owner chose.
